segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: What you're looking at on screen is actually an overview of how much money our agency has spent on ads in the last 30 days.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you can't see that, it's over $2.2 million.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, when it comes to media buying, I want you to know that I have tried every single possible way to click buttons and

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: make more money for the brands that we work with as well as for the brands that we consult.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Whenever it comes to buttons that you can click to actually make you more money, there are very few inside of Facebook as of 2025.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The glory days of being able to magically make more money by clicking one button on Facebook unfortunately aren't here.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But there are still a few that if you click them the right way and you structure them the right way, you can actually turn your ad account into

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: a much more profitable and higher-spending machine for your e-commerce brand.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And in this week's video, I'm going to walk through absolutely everything when it comes to how to structure your ad account,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: how to properly creative test, how to scale, what attribution settings you need to use,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and absolutely everything that I can possibly think of, and literally everything that I know about how to spend millions of dollars

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: for your brand inside of Facebook the best possible way right now.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, before I move further into this video, I need to make it clear, even if this means half of you click off:

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: There is no ad account structure that will save your bad ads.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If your offer sucks, your ads suck, and your landing pages are not good, this structure will not save you.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: However, if after implementing everything that I'm going to talk about in this week's video, you still are not able to scale further,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: then it's your sign that it is not your structure that is the problem. It is those three things that I just mentioned.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, as much as I'm excited for you to see everything about how to structure Meta ads the right way—at least if you ask me—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: that if you really want the most out of this structure, you need to put intent and focus into the things that actually matter.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, with all that said, let's go ahead and jump into the video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, first things first: I'm going to be building this in a blank, random ad account.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, again, I do have ad accounts that I will likely pull up to show you the results as we make it through this video,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but I'm going to be building this from scratch to help you guys understand how to set these up properly.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, the thing that I want to clarify right away, and I have to go full screen for this, is that

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: do not turn off all of your campaigns after watching this video to set up your campaigns and do everything that I show you in this video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you decide to do that and your performance tanks, that is 100% your fault. Okay? Do not turn off—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: we have one golden rule at the agency, and that rule is if something is working, just leave it on.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Okay? There is no point in turning something off that is making you money. So,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: if you have 100 campaigns or 1,000 campaigns and a whole bunch of crazy stuff all over the place, if it's working, just leave it on.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what I would encourage you to do is to set these campaigns and follow what I mention in this video as addition to whatever you have going on,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because I do not want you to go into your ad account and turn off all your campaigns, tank your ad spend and tank your performance, and say,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: "Well, this ad strategy didn't work." Well, it's not supposed to replace everything overnight, okay? This is a gradual process

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: to get your account structured the right way, but I just want to make that clear before we actually get into this.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Before we even talk about getting everything set up, the first thing that you actually need to set up is your columns.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And you need to understand that your columns are what communicate data to you.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, if you do not have your columns set up and you do not have these custom metrics that I'm about to explain to you, you need to get them set up

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because they are very, very important for you to actually be able to look at the data in your account and actually get more from the data that Facebook is communicating to you.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, if you want our exact columns, what you're going to do is just take a screenshot of this, or pause the video, and you can see the exact columns that we use:

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: things like campaign name, ad set name, attribution setting, budget, and we have some custom metrics down here as well like conversion rate, or hook rate, and hold rate.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And some of these you guys might be familiar with, but I want you to basically just pause the video, you can see these are the columns that we use.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And again, if you want to find them, for example, you just search them up here, click CPM, and then you can click save.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, I'm not going to explain what every single one of these mean, but what I will do is show you the custom metrics. So, the custom metrics that we actually make for our brands

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: are very simple, okay? So, the first one is going to be CVR. So, if we actually look down here, you can see we have CVR.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what CVR is, is very simply purchases divided by landing page views. You could also do purchases divided by link clicks, but if you've never made a custom metric in your life,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: you're just going to come in here and search up what it is that I showed you, which the first one is going to be purchases, and then you're going to do divided by,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and then the next one here is again going to be landing page views. And then when you're naming this, again, you could call this Purchase CVR,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and you're going to change this into a percentage, because obviously this is a percentage that you're looking at, and you can make this access to, or you know, basically give access to everybody,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and then you're going to click create metric. Now, I'm not going to do that, cuz I already have the metric, but the other two metrics that we have are video hold.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, video hold is very simple: ThruPlays divided by impressions. And what this tells us is how many people watch

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: 15 seconds of my video ad and so throughplays basically just means 15 seconds

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and if your ad is shorter than 15 seconds, then you're simply just going to see how many people watch the entire thing. That's what video hold is.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then hook rate is a very common one, this is just three-second video plays / impressions.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, from there, those are the custom metrics that we set up. We used to create a custom metric

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: called AOV, but Facebook has since actually come up with their own, it's called average purchase conversion value, and again I will show you where all of these things come

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: into play. Now from there, another thing that is super important for you to have

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is the actual indication of what your audiences are, because this is a lot of times when we see media buyers make the mistake,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: where they will say this is a broad ad set, that is for let's just say women

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: who are 35+, right? And that's what they will call their ad set. Now

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: if you don't have these columns added, which again if you go into the customized columns here, you can see we have these additional columns here, we can see that we have gender

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: as a indicator, we have audience as an indicator, and we have age as an indicator, and this is super important to have this here,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because this is the data that is actually being pulled from what you have selected. And so, as you can see,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: my media buyer, or me in this instance, wrote broad ad set women 35+,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but we can see, because I have my column set up the right way, we're actually targeting both genders and it's 18 to 65, it's not 35+. So, now we're

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: able to easily catch mistakes, and this is going to be super common when we get into the excluded audiences and the included audiences, because we see so many times

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: media buyers accidentally include audiences rather than exclude them. So it's very, very important that you have this here

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: so you can see the data on the ad set level. And then again from the ad side, there's no data here,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but just know that seeing the metrics of conversion rate and average order value really help you understand

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: where your ad is performing well. Same thing with hook rate and hold rate, this just gives you a better idea of how well your ads are hooking

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: in your audience, and how good of a job it's actually doing of keeping them watching that video, and we also like video average play time, because this just gives us a rough estimate of where people are stopping

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and where we likely need to fix the video, or just before that, in order to give them a reason

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: to keep watching. So, that is all of the columns that we have, and again I know we haven't even got into the structure yet,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: there's going to be a lot to cover in this video. But again, your data is your truth, so it is very important that you have things structured and set up the right

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: way. Now, the next thing that you need to do, unlike me in this example,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is you need to name your campaigns, you need to name your ad sets, and most importantly you need to name your ads,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because as you saw over here, in my reporting section, what's really cool about this is our agency actually has the

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: ability to come through here and start to filter specific things by their name. So, if you're not actually putting

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: time and attention into naming your ads properly, and including variables like this is a video,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: or this is an iteration, or this is an ideation, or even things as granular like we do based off of editors or based off of, if you're a really big brand,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: specific agencies or in-house teams that you're working with, and it's so valuable to actually take the time

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: to name your ad sets so again you have clarity and you can be organized in the account. Lucky for you,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: if you are watching this video, I will actually attach a naming scheme that we use down below. It's a little bit

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: complex so you can feel free to simplify it, but if you just want to copy the naming scheme that we have used before, I will give that to you guys and you guys are more than welcome to take that

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and install that into your business, because you just need to make sure that you have some kind of naming scheme rather than none at all. You have no idea how many times I do audits on brands

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: where they just have things like "New sales ad" and "New sales ad copy", and they have no idea what's going on,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: they can't pull reports properly, and again your data is your truth, so it is so important to make sure

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: that you know what is going on. So, bare minimum, make sure you name your ads, and ideally you name everything and you stay

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: organized so that way you don't have to click into everything, and again you can always double check by having specific columns set up

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: like this where you can see your exclusions, inclusions, and all of that kind of stuff. Now this is great and all, but let's talk about the juicy stuff

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: which is actually going to be the structure, okay? The structure that we are going to be setting up is going to be

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: the 3-2-2-2 structure. Now, you've probably heard of the 3-2-2 before,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: which was made famous by Charley T, and he is kind of like the godfather of that, and we have a lot of respect for Charley,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: but we've kind of implemented a little bit of our own spice onto this by adding an additional two at the end, which also includes testing specific landing pages.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if you are a brand that is spending less than a thousand dollars per day,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: you should honestly never have more than one campaign, maybe max two.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And the reason for that is because you need all of your budget as consolidated as possible, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You need as much spend going into your ads as you can get,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because as soon as you start to spread your spend super thin, it just makes it extremely hard for Meta to optimize.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, the only two campaigns you should ever have are the 3-2-2-2 campaign that I'm about to show you how to set up, as well as a potential ASC campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: With that said, what we're going to do here is we're going to set up our campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So you're going to create a new campaign, and I'll actually do this one from scratch with you,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and what you're going to do is you're going to, obviously, select Sales.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Once you select Sales, you're going to click Continue, and here you're just going to select Manual Sales campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: For now, we will come back to the Advantage+ Shopping, we're going to click Continue.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And now, again, you're going to name things properly, and just as a small thing, templates are also awesome.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You can create your own templates inside of Meta if you want.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And we're going to call this our Acquisition campaign, and that's a word that I always spell wrong.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But we're going to call this Acquisition, where it's going to be a US CBO, kind of alluding there, and this is usually what most of our campaigns look like.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And inside of here, again, buying type is just going to be Auction, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The campaign objective is Sales, the campaign spending limit is just going to be None. We're not going to run catalog ads, we're going to run Advantage campaign budget.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: With that said, if you are a brand that is multi-SKU,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: we can talk about catalog ads after, there's going to be a little mini Q&A section that I'm going to get to,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: for any common questions or most frequently asked questions that we get.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But the most important thing here is we're going to turn on CBO.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, for those of you that don't like CBO or think ABO is better,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I'm going to try to give you an example that will hopefully hit home and help you shift your perspective on why we usually do everything in CBO rather than ABO.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Number one: for those of you that are super stuck with making sure that your ads get spend, you can actually run minimum budgets inside of CBO campaigns,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: so it basically gives you the best of both worlds.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you have a larger budget of say $5,000 or $10,000 or $100,000 a day, you can set minimum budgets on each and every single creative.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then get the added benefit of CBO with whatever excess spend that you have, it will just go towards your top ads.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So if you're still ride or die for ABO because you're able to force spend, there's no point. You can just run CBO with minimum budget, which is something that we are going to discuss.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And the second reason, which should hopefully make a lot of sense, is because Meta has invested billions of dollars at this point building an AI algorithm.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what this algorithm does is it analyzes ads every single day and knows and has a pretty good idea of what ads are going to perform in the auction and what ads are not.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so this is why they came out with this thing called Advantage+ Budget Optimization or Advantage Campaign Budget.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what it's doing is it's leveraging its AI and its algorithm to basically analyze your ads and figure out which ones are actually going to perform.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And now I know somebody's like, "Thanks for explaining the obvious." And I know, I just need to make sure that we're on the same page.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But more importantly, you need to understand that this algorithm performs a lot like your favorite TikTok algorithm or the Instagram algorithm where you get served things that you like, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Just like how you loaded up a YouTube video, and now you're watching this video because you're interested in e-commerce, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: YouTube has an algorithm that understands you, all right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And just like how an organic algorithm will recommend videos to you, for example, have videos that go viral, they go viral because they are good.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And the platform is pushing it organically because it is good.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: It's the exact same thing inside of Facebook with its ad algorithm.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You don't need to force spend on 99% of your ads because Meta has an algorithm that knows what's going to be good, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, just like how when you post an organic video, if it completely flops, it was probably just a bad video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then on the other side, if you post a video organically and it goes viral and it gets a ton of views, it was probably a pretty good video, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, for some reason, us marketers think we're smarter than the machine, and we think that because Meta is not spending on our ads—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: aka in the organic version they're not going viral—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: we think Facebook is wrong, and that we're smarter, and that it needs to spend on that ad.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Meanwhile, every time we do that or majority of the time that we do that, it just actually doesn't perform.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, the thing that happens to so many people is the odd time you will actually see an ad start to get some decent performance on ABO when you force budget to it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But the truth is is it rarely ever scales your account, it rarely ever goes viral,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and again, the example of the organic algorithm, and that's the—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: problem. We are leveraging Facebook to be able to scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So I don't really care if an ad gets two purchases a day when I have ads that are getting me 200 a day that Meta is spending all of my budget on.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, hopefully that example, I know it was a little, maybe a little bit hard to follow, but the example of the organic algorithm pushing videos that go viral is the exact same as Meta putting spend on your best videos because it has the same algorithm. It knows what's good, and it's going to push it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so there's no need to really waste a ton of budget on testing your creatives just because you think they're good.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And I promise that is the end of the CBO/ABO rant.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you still want to test ABO after this, be my guest. I'm not going to tell you that you're wrong.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I'm just explaining from my side of things and trying to help you understand the actual facts around why Meta developed this and why it's actually encouraged for you to use it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: A lot of times, our egos just get in the way, and that's why we default it to forcing spend, but at the end of it all, hopefully that makes sense.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now that we got over the big ABO question, we can get into the rest of the setup, which is going to be setting a daily budget.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, set the daily budget to whatever you are comfortable with. I'm just going to throw this at $200 per day.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, this is something that I do want to call out as well, because Meta has actually moved to a weekly budget, similar to how Google functions, rather than a daily budget.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, that's why some of you guys will set a budget of $200 per day, and sometimes it spends more than that, as you can see here, it says it may spend up to 350.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And that's because Meta is now trying to spot the days that are really good for performance and just have more wiggle room to spend more on those days.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, make sure you keep an eye on this, because sometimes Meta has had some weird overspending things happening as they've started to roll this out.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But just so you are clear on what this actually means, Meta will not always spend $200 per day, but by the end of the week, it will likely stay within the $1,400 budget.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, when it comes to campaign bid strategy, I know this is another massive topic of bid caps or cost per results or ROAS goals,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and I'll be 100% honest with you, we are simply just running highest volume or value.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, this is actually something new that Meta came out with, where it used to be go for highest volume or go for highest value, and they've kind of merged the two together.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But the most important thing here is you need to understand what this is telling the machine.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: This is telling the machine that we want it to go and get the highest volume of purchases or the highest value of purchases every single day.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, there are a lot of bid cap and cost cap warriors that love to talk about their cost caps and love to talk about their bid caps,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and you know what? I will give them the ability to go and rave about them.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I don't really care about the people that run bid caps or cost caps. They can do that if they please.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The biggest thing that I want to clarify is that cost caps and bid caps are not going to save your bad ads.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Again, media buying is simply supporting you. It's not driving the performance; it's supporting the performance.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, so many people think it's because their cost cap wasn't set properly or their bid cap wasn't set properly, and that's why they haven't been able to scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: No, it's just because your ads aren't that good or your offer isn't that good. That's why they're not scaling.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And because we run in CBO and we do not waste spend on bad ads, we, a lot of the times, don't really need cost caps or bid caps to test our creatives or run our campaigns, because we just let the algorithm do its thing.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, if you want to run cost caps and you want to run bid caps, you totally can, but we honestly don't.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And we have honestly tested them. We've tried these crazy, inflated budget strategies. We've tried doing all these different cost caps and bid caps, and it's just, honestly, it's just a waste of time.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I'd rather see you spend an entire day making better ads than spend an entire day playing with bids and cost caps.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you were to ask me who's going to win: bid cap or cost cap keyboard warrior or a marketer that just spends the entire day making great ads,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: the marketer is going to win 100 times out of 100 because, again, Facebook is just a tool for marketing,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: right? So, if you have great marketing, it doesn't matter what you optimize the machine with, you're going to perform well.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now again, we're going to continue through this, but those two big things between ABO and CBO and cost caps, bid caps, or highest volume, they always get people all fired up, but at the end of the day, it's not what makes or breaks your account, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, hopefully that makes sense, and you can go back to focusing on creatives, offers, and landing pages because those are what's actually going to scale your account and ideally get you to where you want to go, not really the cost caps.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Okay. So now that we're on highest volume or value, and I've probably lost half of the audience because I'm not talking about some crazy bid cap strategy,

segments.speaker: Presenter
